requirement_text.REQ-364:
Implements REQ-363's design artefact exactly — no new schema decisions here, this requirement is implementation of an already-validated design, matching this project's own CODE-DESIGNER-then-ELIXIR-DEV split for every other schema-bearing feature.

SCOPE: the `Letflow.Help` context module (naming follows this project's existing per-domain-context convention, e.g. `Letflow.Identity`, `Letflow.TenantProvisioning`) exposing: create a draft, update a draft, publish (draft -> live, sets confirmed_at), re-confirm (bumps confirmed_at on an already-live row without changing body — the explicit "I checked this, it's still accurate" action), and read (by screen_id + tenant prefix, or by process_definition_id). Every write path enforces REQ-363's sanitization rule from that design, not a weakened version of it.

NOT IN SCOPE: the tenant-facing authoring UI (REQ-365 for platform, a separate future requirement for the tenant admin UI itself — this requirement's acceptance criteria stop at a working, tested context module, callable from IEx/tests, not yet wired to any HTTP route or frontend component). Route/controller wiring, if this project's own API-surface convention wants a separate requirement for it (matching the pattern most REQ-027..030-style definition CRUD work already used), is a natural fast-follow, not bundled here — state explicitly in this requirement's close-out whether a route was added or deliberately deferred, rather than leaving it ambiguous.

task.description: Validate CODE-DESIGNER's amended req363-help-content-data-model.md section 5.4 (the AST-based sanitizer CODE-DESIGNER wrote per REVIEWER's step-03d determination, replacing the rejected regex-denylist approach). Section 5.4's href/src attribute-list claims are independently verified, not merely secondary-sourced
No implementation code appears in the design (signatures/shapes only)
The new dependency (earmark_parser) is flagged for REVIEWER sign-off

result.summary:
RECONSTRUCTION NOTE: this handoff was originally written live during WF02-REQ364-20260917's security-review saga as ad-hoc, non-schema JSON (informal top-level keys such as req/at/result-as-bare-string instead of HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §2's real schema), the exact anti-pattern this session's own ISS-0692 precedent names. It has been rewritten into full schema conformance by a later ORCH session under §4.1's not_agent_attested mechanism. created_at/started_at/completed_at are all set to the file's own git-introducing-commit timestamp (`git log --follow --diff-filter=A --format=%aI --reverse -- <path>`), the best-available real timestamp, NOT the original live dispatch/claim/completion times, which were never recorded in schema-legal fields on disk. All findings, quoted test counts, and verification detail below are migrated verbatim in substance from the original ad-hoc file; nothing was invented or paraphrased away.

BLOCKING FINDING: SS5.4.2 step 2 misdescribes earmark_parser's actual AST shape for raw HTML as a 'separately-tagged node kind' -- verified against real hexdocs/README that raw/verbatim HTML is NOT a distinct tag/node kind. Every node is a uniform 4-tuple {tag, attrs, children, meta}; raw HTML is marked by meta[:verbatim] == true on a node that otherwise carries an ordinary-looking tag (e.g. {"span", [...], [...], %{verbatim: true}}). A reasonable implementer following the design as written would branch on node tag/shape, not meta[:verbatim], silently reopening a raw-HTML bypass -- the exact failure mode recurring at the design layer instead of the regex layer.

REQUIRED FIX: Correct SS5.4.2 step 2 to name the real discriminator (meta[:verbatim] == true on the walked node). Re-verify step 3's href/src attribute-list claim against the same primary source, since it was checked via the same secondary-fetch method as the now-disproven step 2 claim.

NON-BLOCKING NOTE: SS5.4.1's 'earmark depends on earmark_parser' lineage claim is directionally true (earmark_parser's own README self-describes as extracted from earmark) but overstated against current hex.pm data -- earmark 1.4.49 lists zero deps and its GitHub repo is archived/retired. Should say 'originally extracted from' rather than 'depends on', and flag to REVIEWER that earmark itself (not earmark_parser) is retired, for due-diligence context even though this design correctly avoids taking earmark as a dependency.

CONFIRMED GOOD: earmark_parser confirmed real (hex.pm, Apache-2.0, zero runtime deps, actively maintained, 16 dependents including ex_doc). No implementation code found in SS5.4. New-dependency flag for REVIEWER sign-off present and correctly framed.

issues.description: SS5.4.2 step 2 misdescribes earmark_parser's raw-HTML AST shape as a distinct tagged node kind; the real discriminator is meta[:verbatim] == true on an otherwise ordinary node, and a reasonable implementer following the design as written would reopen a raw-HTML bypass.
SS5.4.1's 'earmark depends on earmark_parser' phrasing overstates current reality (earmark itself is retired/archived, earmark_parser has zero runtime deps); should read 'originally extracted from'.

result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER -- correct SS5.4.2 step 2's AST-shape claim and re-verify SS5.4 step 3, rework iteration 1 of 3.
